SOAP Clinical Note

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: Tight sensation in chest for the past 3 hours.
- Associated symptoms:
  • Mild shortness of breath (worse on exertion, not at rest).  
  • Wheeze.  
  • Non-productive cough, slightly worse at night, persisting since a viral upper-respiratory infection last week (previous sore throat/runny nose now improving).  
  • No chest “pain,” only tightness; no sputum production.
- Past medical history:
  • Asthma (severe exacerbation requiring intubation and inpatient stay at age 16–17).  
  • Childhood eczema.  
  • Childhood milk-protein allergy (resolved).  
  • Allergic rhinitis/hay fever.
- Surgical history: None mentioned.
- Medications:
  • Salbutamol (Ventolin) inhaler – ran out 1 week ago; dose/route/frequency not documented.  
  • Beclomethasone dipropionate (Clenil Modulite) inhaler – ran out 1 week ago; dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Allergies: No known drug allergies; environmental allergy to dust.
- Family history: Father – asthma; Mother – eczema.
- Social history: University student (away at university last week); smoking status not discussed.

Objective:
- Remote consultation – no vitals or physical examination performed.
- No investigations performed.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Acute asthma exacerbation
   - Assessment: Mild–moderate acute asthma exacerbation likely precipitated by recent viral URTI and lapse in controller/reliever inhaler use.
   - Investigations planned: None immediate; consider peak-flow monitoring if available.
   - Treatment planned:
     • Oral corticosteroid course: Prednisolone (exact dose not documented) – 2 tablets each morning for 5 days.  
     • Restart controller inhaler: Beclomethasone (Clenil Modulite).  
     • Reliever inhaler: Salbutamol (Ventolin) PRN; advise medical review if required more frequently than every 3 hours.  
     • Spacer device prescribed with usage instructions.  
   - Safety-net advice: Seek urgent medical attention for worsening shortness of breath, increasing chest tightness/pain, need for Ventolin > q3h, light-headedness, or other concerning symptoms.

2. Medication refill / Prescription request
   - Assessment: Out of both reliever and controller inhalers.
   - Treatment planned: Electronic prescriptions sent for Salbutamol inhaler, Clenil Modulite inhaler, 5-day oral steroid course, and spacer.

3. Work / activity advice
   - Assessment: Needs time to rest while recovering from exacerbation.
   - Treatment planned: Advised patient may self-certify for first 7 days; rest recommended until symptoms improve.

Quality checks:
● Missing but expected elements: No vitals, peak-flow reading, smoking status, drug doses/frequencies.  
● Internal conflicts: None noted.  
● Transcript quality: Clear; occasional minor audio dropouts but did not affect key clinical content.
